summary: Seiji Nemoto is a scholar in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Meiji University (~1968–1972) and served as a professor at the University of Tsukuba (~2001–2015).
Seiji Tanaka studied under Bruno Petzold and worked in other fields. He held academic posts at Asia University and Aoyama Gakuin University (~1968–1978).
Seijun Ishii is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University (~1977–1987). He later served as a professor at Komazawa University (~2004).

Seijun Sato was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University. He held positions at Taisho University and served as representative at Ishigami Zen'nō Kyōju Koki Kinen Ronbunshū Kankōkai (~2001).

Seikaku Hirata was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1946–1950) under Shin'ichi Hisamatsu, as well as under Bokuo Seki. He taught Prabhasa Dharma and held a post at Hanazono University.

Sein Tin was active in linguistics and other fields. He studied at Basic Education High School No. 9 Mawlamyine, the University of Rangoon (~1917–1921), Christ Church, Oxford (~1921–1923), and under Pe Maung Tin (1924–1927).

Seiran Ouchi was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who founded Hoshi Sodan (1874) and Meikyo Shinshi (1875). He held a post at Nishi Hongan-ji, served as president of Toyo University (1914–1918), and taught Totsudo Kato.

Seiren Matsunami was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo until 1930, under Naoshiro Tsuji and Walther Schubring. He held posts at Kyushu University, Rissho University (attested 1972), and Taisho University (attested 1972).

Seishi Karashima was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology. He studied at the University of Tokyo, Cambridge, and Peking University under mentors including von Hinüber and Ji Xianlin. He held posts at the Eastern Institute and Soka University.

Seishin Kato was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Toyo University and Shingiyaha Daigakurin. He served as president of Buzan University (1918, 1923) and Toyo University (1952, 1955), and held posts at Taisho, Tokyo, and Rissho universities.
Seitatsu Matsunami is an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. He served as an assistant at the University of Tokyo and as a professor at Taisho University (attested 1992).

Seizan Yanagida worked in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Hanazono, Otani, and Kyoto universities under Kaiten Nukariya and Shin'ichi Hisamatsu. He held posts at Hanazono University, Kyoto University (1976–1986), and Chubu University (~1986–1992).

Semen Ivanovich Tyulyaev was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Moscow State University (~1921–1927) and held posts at the State Museum of Oriental Art (1927–1958) and the Institute of Oriental Studies (1958–1961).

Sempa Dorje is a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Ram Shankar Tripathi (attested 1977) and served as a professor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 1977, 1990–1998).
Semën Gesselevič Rudin was an Indologist and linguist. He completed his studies at Saint Petersburg State University (1947–1952, ~1963–1968) and held a post there beginning in 1955.
Sen Wang was a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Peking University (~1932–1936) and served as a professor at Minzu University of China (~1952–1961).

Senarat Wijayasundara is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. In 1999, he was attested as a teacher at the University of Kelaniya and as a visiting lecturer at the Buddhist and Pali College of Singapore.
Senarath Paranavitana worked in history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Jean Philippe Vogel (~1935–1936) and held a post at Leiden University (~1935–1936).

Senchu Murano is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Rissho University (~1929–1933) and the University of Washington (~1935–1938), and later served as a professor at Rissho University (~1958–1979).

Sengaku Mayeda was an Indologist, philosopher, and Buddhist scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Pennsylvania under W. Norman Brown, among others. He taught at Tokyo, Pennsylvania, Gakushuin, Keio, and Musashino universities.
